answer: A new identity in the agent economy starts hollow: zero weight, no voting power, no reward share — like a lotus seed that has not yet bloomed. Weight only grows when the agent completes verifiable useful work for real counterparties and those counterparties attest it on a public ledger, the way a meadow fills in one plant at a time. A sybil attacker must therefore do genuine, paid-for work for every fake identity, and the work costs more than the reward the fake identity can extract. Cheap identities stay hollow forever; expensive ones are no longer cheap.
